details:
NISEarth: What the Radar Saw

NISEarth is an interactive, open-source platform that helps users explore how Earth’s surface changes over time using radar data from the NASA–ISRO NISAR mission.

The application brings together cases from Spain and other regions, covering floods, wildfires, landslides, earthquakes, volcanic activity and land subsidence. Users can navigate a 3D globe, compare radar images from different dates and examine time series and maps of observed changes. For selected cases, the platform also displays ground movement derived from radar interferometry.

NISEarth combines these observations with other geographic and environmental data, including rainfall, land cover, infrastructure and population estimates. By bringing multiple datasets into the same scenario, users can explore possible relationships—for example, between ground movement and rainfall—and develop questions for further investigation. Selected results can also be compared with external sources such as Copernicus EMS, EFFIS and NASA FIRMS.

The platform includes a guided story mode, a hazard guide and downloadable reports with maps, charts, methods and sources. It is available in English and Spanish.

Our longer-term goal is to use these combined datasets to investigate correlations and support estimates and predictions. The current application is an exploratory tool: correlations do not establish causation, and satellite observations depend on data availability, acquisition timing and the limitations of each method.
